text:
Tyson Foerster's slow start has been a Philadelphia storyline; the Inquirer and the Delco Times both wrote about it last week. He's answered with 7 points in his last ten games, including a goal and two assists in Thursday's win in Ottawa, where his goal came 15 seconds after Rodrigo York's.

The season line, 5 goals and 10 points in 24 games, is in line with his chances. He's scored about what his expected goals say, and his shooting is at 10.6%, a bit below the 12% to 17% range we'd expect from someone with his release (his hardest shot sits in the 96th percentile). He played just 29 games last season, and he's back at about 17 minutes a night with four power-play points.

The concern is five on five, where the Flyers take only about 44% of the expected goals with him on the ice. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking shows a dump-and-chase game: he carries the puck in on just 31% of his entries. The shot is the weapon; the even-strength play is what we'd watch.
headline: Tyson Foerster is shooting his way back
